updates.title: Inventory opens on the Active tab, with the Inactive tab beside it
preconditions: You are signed in as an Admin at {Location-A} (for example Staging Heavy Duty - 9919). The Admin role has 'Part Library & Inventory → View / Create & Edit / Delete'.
Inventory part {Part-A} (for example ZZAUTOTEST-PL-TABS-01) is active and tracked at {Location-A}.
steps: In the top bar click Parts, then click Inventory in the left menu.
Look at the area between the page title "Inventory" and the table.
results: Step 1: The Inventory page opens with two tabs, "Active" and "Inactive", and "Active" is already the selected tab (shown in blue) without you clicking it.

Step 2: The two tabs sit on their own line directly under the title "Inventory". The search and filter row (Search, Bin Location, Category, Supply, the columns icon, the ⋮ menu and New Inventory Part) sits below the tabs, not beside them.
Step 3: The Active tab lists {Part-A} (1 row).
Step 4: "Inactive" becomes the selected tab and {Part-A} is not listed there.
Step 5: "Active" is selected again and {Part-A} is listed again.

updates.title: Parts that existed before the release are active and tracked
preconditions: You are signed in as an Admin at {Location-A} (for example Staging Heavy Duty - 9919). The Admin role has 'Part Library & Inventory → View / Create & Edit / Delete'.

Inventory parts {Part-A}, {Part-B} and {Part-C} (for example ZZAUTOTEST-PL-RELEASE-01, -02 and -03) existed at {Location-A} before the Part Lifecycle build was deployed, and nobody has changed them since.
Part {Part-B} has a quantity above 0 and a saved Min and Max (for example Min 1 and Max 6).
You can pick a second location, {Location-B} (for example Staging Lethbridge - 4310), in the location selector.
steps: In the top bar click Parts, then click Inventory in the left menu.
Type {Part-A} in the Search box, replacing any text there.
Type {Part-B} in the Search box, replacing any text there.
Open Settings and look through its menu, including the Parts group and Roles & Permissions, for an on or off setting for the Active and Inactive tabs or for tracking.
In the top bar click Parts, then click Inventory in the left menu.
results: Steps 2 to 4: Each of {Part-A}, {Part-B} and {Part-C} is listed on the Active tab, and its Total Qty column shows a number, never "Not Tracked".
Steps 6 to 8: None of the three is listed on the Inactive tab.

Step 11: Edit Inventory Part opens with a green "Active" pill in the title row, Part Status set to Active, and the "Track quantities and cost of goods" switch on, with Min and Max showing the values {Part-B} had before the deployment (for example 1 and 6).
Step 13: There is no setting that turns the Active and Inactive tabs or tracking on or off: the feature is simply on.
Step 15: {Location-B} also shows the Active and Inactive tabs.
updates.source: Epic SV-10647; story SV-10814 (Story 1, Active and Inactive Tabs on the Inventory List); PRD "Parts Lifecycle Update", Confluence 829227015, v29 (14 Oct 2026 copy), S1-R5, S1-R5a, S1-R5b, S13-R3, S4-R8, read 14 Oct 2026; design canvas board 3.1 (Part Status in the dialog), board 5.3 (The list says Not Tracked), 13 Oct copy. updates.title: Each tab lists only the parts with that status at the current location
preconditions: You are signed in as an Admin who can pick two locations in the location selector, {Location-A} (for example Staging Heavy Duty - 9919) and {Location-B} (for example Staging Lethbridge - 4310). The Admin role has 'Part Library & Inventory → View / Create & Edit / Delete'.
Inventory part {Part-A} (for example ZZAUTOTEST-PL-LOCTAB-01) is active at {Location-A} and is not stocked at {Location-B}.
Inventory part {Part-B} (for example ZZAUTOTEST-PL-LOCTAB-02) is stocked at both locations with the same part number: inactive at {Location-A} and active at {Location-B}.
Both part numbers start with the same text, {Prefix-A} (for example ZZAUTOTEST-PL-LOCTAB).
steps: Pick {Location-A} in the location selector in the top bar.
In the top bar click Parts, then click Inventory in the left menu.
In the top bar click Parts, then click Inventory in the left menu.

results: Step 3: At {Location-A} the Active tab lists {Part-A} and does not list {Part-B}: 1 row.
Step 4: At {Location-A} the Inactive tab lists {Part-B} and does not list {Part-A}: 1 row.
Step 7: At {Location-B} the Active tab lists {Part-B}, because it is still active there: 1 row. {Part-A} is not listed, because it is not stocked at {Location-B}.

quotes: S1-R3
The Active tab lists only parts that are active at the current location.
S1-R4
The Inactive tab lists only parts that are inactive at the current location.
PRD §2 Feature Overview (Core functionality)
Both states belong to the part at one location. The same part at another location keeps its own states.
PRD §4 Key Decisions (Active and tracked are set per location)

Active and tracked are set per location. A part is stocked at a location, and whether the shop still sells it, or counts it, is that location's call. Changing either state at one location never changes the same part at another location.

updates.title: Changing an entry's number on the Part Library page renames the part
preconditions: You are signed in as an Admin who can pick two locations in the location selector, {Location-A} (for example Staging Heavy Duty - 9919) and {Location-B} (for example Staging Lethbridge - 4310). The Admin role has 'Part Library & Inventory → View / Create & Edit / Delete'.
Inventory part {Part-A} (for example ZZAUTOTEST-PL-LIBREN-01) is active at both {Location-A} and {Location-B}, on one Part Library entry.
The new number {Number-A} (for example ZZAUTOTEST-PL-LIBREN-01N) is not used by any Part Library entry.
steps: Pick {Location-A} in the location selector in the top bar.
In the top bar click Parts, then click Part Library in the left menu.
Click the pencil icon beside the entry's name in the Part details panel.
Replace the Part Number with {Part-A} again.
In the top bar click Parts, then click Part Library in the left menu.
In the top bar click Parts, then click Inventory in the left menu.
Click the clock icon (tooltip "Part History") at the left of the {Number-A} row.
In the top bar click Parts, then click Inventory in the left menu.
Click the clock icon at the left of the {Number-A} row.
results: Step 6: Under the Part Number field the dialog shows "This also changes the part number at 1 other location."
Step 7: With the saved number typed back, the message disappears.
Step 8: The message shows again.
Step 9: The change is saved and the detail page shows {Number-A}.
Step 11: No entry is found for {Part-A}: no new Part Library entry was created for the old number.
Step 12: One entry is found, {Number-A}.
Step 14: At {Location-A} the Inventory list shows the part as {Number-A} (the same part, with the same stock), and {Part-A} is no longer listed.
Step 15: Part History at {Location-A} has a new entry "Part number updated | Original number: {Part-A} | New number: {Number-A}" with your name, today's date and time, and no "Changed at" at the end.
Step 18: At {Location-B} the same part is listed as {Number-A}.

Step 19: Part History at {Location-B} has the entry "Part number updated | Original number: {Part-A} | New number: {Number-A} | Changed at: {Location-A}", with the name of {Location-A} as the location selector shows it.

quotes: S11-R3a
Changing an entry's number or description on its detail page follows the part dialog's rules: S13-R12 to S13-R19, S13-N1, S13-N7, and S10-R23 to S10-R25.

When the user changes the part number and at least one other location stocks the same Part Library entry, the dialog shows, under the field, "This also changes the part number at {n} other locations.", or "This also changes the part number at 1 other location." for one.
That message shows only while the typed number differs from the saved one, ignoring spaces before and after it. Parts at other locations count whether they are active or inactive.

Saving a changed number renames the part in place. The part keeps its identity, its history, and every line that holds it. Its Part Library entry is renamed with it, and its core takes the same number. No new Part Library entry is created.
A changed part number writes "Part number updated | Original number: {old} | New number: {new}" to the Part History of the part at every location that stocks it.
On the entries written at the other locations, the line ends with "| Changed at: {location}", naming the location where the change was made.

Inventory part {Part-A} (for example ZZAUTOTEST-PL-REQMSG-01) is active at {Location-A}, so it is also a Part Library entry.
Work order {Work-order-1} (for example S2-15440) is open, for a ZZAUTOTEST customer, with a line {Line-1} (for example "ZZAUTOTEST PL request message line").
steps: In the top bar click Work Orders.
In the Parts row of {Line-1} click + Add Part.
In New Part Request, type {Part-A} in Part Number.
Pick the result whose source reads "Part Library".
Read the Source and Category fields.
results: Step 6: Source and Category are filled in for the part picked from the Part Library.
Step 7: The part request is saved on {Line-1} with no error message.

Steps 5 to 7: The two refusals "Part Library entry missing category." and "A part from the Part Library must have Vendor as its source." (red error toasts that close after about 3 seconds) belong to requests that reach the system with no category or with another source, which this screen does not send: write "refusal wording not checked by hand" in the result comment.

updates.title: The parts import puts a tracked part with no bin into an Unassigned bin
preconditions: You are signed in as an Admin at {Location-A} (for example Staging Heavy Duty - 9919). The Admin role has 'Part Library & Inventory → View / Create & Edit / Delete' and opens Settings → Data Import.
No part numbered {Part-A} (for example ZZAUTOTEST-PL-NOBIN-01) exists at {Location-A}.
Import file {Import-file-A} has one row for {Part-A} with the grid_location cell (the import's name for Bin Location) left empty.
You have noted whether the bin locations of {Location-A} (Settings → Bin Locations) already include one named "Unassigned".
steps: In the top bar click Parts, then click Inventory in the left menu.
results: Step 5: {Part-A} is listed once. Its Bin Location / Quantity column shows the bin "Unassigned" with quantity 0, and its Total Qty shows a quantity, not "Not Tracked".

Step 6: Edit Inventory Part shows "Track quantities and cost of goods" on and, under Inventory, one bin location, "Unassigned", with Quantity 0, marked "Default". A tracked {Part-A} saved with no bin location at all fails the case.
Step 9: Exactly one bin location named "Unassigned" is listed. If there was none before the import, the import created it.

Steps 1 to 9: The refusals for a tracked part that reaches the system with bins but none marked as the default ("At least one bin must be marked as default.") and for a request to turn tracking on for a part with no bin ("At least one bin must be provided.") cannot be produced from the screens. Write "not checked by hand" for them in the result comment.
updates.source: Epic SV-10647; story SV-10817 (Story 4, Create an Untracked Part); story SV-10818 (Story 5, Change Tracking on an Existing Part); story SV-10820 (Story 7, Create a Part by Typing Its Number and Description); PRD "Parts Lifecycle Update", Confluence 829227015, v29 (14 Oct 2026 copy), S4-R7, S4-N1, S4-N2, S5-N1, §8 User Feedback Summary, S7-N10, read 14 Oct 2026; design canvas board 1.1 (New Inventory Part opens), 13 Oct copy. QA lead's 9 Oct set-up answer 2 (an import with Grid Location empty). Product's answer of 13 Oct (Chris Ward, question 3a). Source-verified 14 October 2026; not yet build-verified (no Part Lifecycle QA build exists).
quotes: An import row that adds a tracked part with no bin location puts the part in a bin named "Unassigned", which the import creates at the location if it is missing. On a new part that bin is the default bin.
S4-R7
When the switch is on, at least one bin location must be set, and one must be marked as the default, before the part can be saved.
S4-N1
If a tracked part reaches the system with no bin location, the save is refused with "At least one bin must be provided."
S4-N2
If a tracked part reaches the system with bin locations but none marked as the default, the save is refused with "At least one bin must be marked as default."
S5-N1
If a request to turn tracking on reaches the system with no bin location, it is refused with "At least one bin must be provided." The dialog never sends one, because of S5-R7.
PRD Story 4 context note
in the dialog a new part always starts with the location's default bin, and the last bin and the default bin cannot be removed, so S4-N1 and S4-N2 come from requests made outside the dialog.
PRD §8 User Feedback Summary (Tracked part saved with no bin)
"At least one bin must be provided." | Error toast, fades after 3 seconds
PRD §8 User Feedback Summary (Tracked part saved with no default bin)
"At least one bin must be marked as default." | Error toast, fades after 3 seconds
PRD §8 User Feedback Summary (context note)
every refusal sent by the system, the rows that fade after 3 seconds, also shows a second, smaller line under the message: "Please try to resolve this."

updates.title: A rename through the public API carries over like a rename in the part dialog
preconditions: You are signed in as an Admin who can pick two locations in the location selector, {Location-A} (for example Staging Heavy Duty - 9919) and {Location-B} (for example Staging Lethbridge - 4310). The Admin role has 'Part Library & Inventory → View / Create & Edit / Delete'.
Inventory part {Part-A} (for example ZZAUTOTEST-PL-PUBAPI-01) is active at both {Location-A} and {Location-B}, on one Part Library entry.
Purchase order {Purchase-order-A} (for example PO-1001) at {Location-A} has an open line for {Part-A}, not yet received.
A connected system has changed {Part-A}'s number to {Number-A} (for example ZZAUTOTEST-PL-PUBAPINEW-02) through ShopView's public API. This cannot be done in the ShopView screens.
steps: Pick {Location-A} in the location selector in the top bar.
In the top bar click Parts, then click Inventory in the left menu.
Click the clock icon (tooltip "Part History") at the left of the {Number-A} row.
In the top bar click Parts, then click Inventory in the left menu.
Click the clock icon at the left of the {Number-A} row.
In the top bar click Parts, then click Purchase Orders in the left menu.
In the top bar click Parts, then click Part Library in the left menu.
results: Step 3: At {Location-A} the part is listed as {Number-A}.
Step 4: Part History at {Location-A} has the entry "Part number updated | Original number: {Part-A} | New number: {Number-A} | Changed through: Public API", with no "Changed at".
Step 8: Part History at {Location-B} has the same entry, also ending "| Changed through: Public API".
Step 11: The open line of {Purchase-order-A} reads {Number-A}.
Step 13: No Part Library entry is found for {Part-A}: the part was renamed in place and no entry was made for the old number.

Steps 1 to 13: This case needs a change made through the public API. If no connected system made it, write "public API change not available, not checked by hand" in the result comment and mark the case Blocked.
updates.source: Epic SV-10647; story SV-10826 (Story 13, The Part Dialog); story SV-10823 (Story 10, Confirming and Recording a Status Change); PRD "Parts Lifecycle Update", Confluence 829227015, v29 (14 Oct 2026 copy), S13-R19d, S13-R18, S13-R19, S10-R23, S10-R25a, read 14 Oct 2026; design canvas: no board shows this behaviour (13 Oct copy). Tech plan "Parts Lifecycle Update — Technical Implementation Plan" (7 Oct 2026), §5 API Changes (public API PATCH). Source-verified 14 October 2026; not yet build-verified (no Part Lifecycle QA build exists).
quotes: A change to a part's number or description made through the public API follows the same rules as the part dialog: S13-R14, S13-R15, S13-R18, S13-R19, S13-N1, S13-N7 and S10-R23 to S10-R25.

Saving a changed number renames the part in place. The part keeps its identity, its history, and every line that holds it. Its Part Library entry is renamed with it, and its core takes the same number. No new Part Library entry is created.

A rename carries over to open work that holds this part, at every location: purchase order lines not yet fully received, part requests not yet received or returned, canned jobs, and returns that are not completed take the new number. A delivery that is not yet accepted is covered by its open purchase order lines. Receiving, ordering, applying a canned job and returning then find the renamed part.
A changed part number writes "Part number updated | Original number: {old} | New number: {new}" to the Part History of the part at every location that stocks it.
Entries written for a change made through the public API end with "| Changed through: Public API" at every location, in place of "| Changed at: {location}".

preconditions: You are signed in as an Admin at {Location-A} (for example Staging Heavy Duty - 9919). The Admin role has 'Part Library & Inventory → View / Create & Edit / Delete'.

steps: In the top bar click Parts, then click Inventory in the left menu.

results: Step 5: When the system answers normally the part is saved. On a server failure a red message "Failed to save part." with "Please try again." fades after about 3 seconds.

Step 9: When the system answers normally a green toast reads "Part deactivated.". On a server failure a red message "Failed to set this part inactive" with "Please try again or contact support for help" fades after about 7 seconds.

Step 13: When the system answers normally the part is deleted and the dialog closes, with no confirmation. On a server failure a red message "Failed to delete part." with "Please try again." fades after about 3 seconds.
Steps 5, 9 and 13: A server failure cannot be caused from the screen: write "server-error messages not checked by hand" in the result comment.

retire.why: Its whole basis left the PRD: it tests a "Deactivate"/"Activate" text control at the left end of the part dialog footer, from the 9 Sep IN-REVIEW draft. The current PRD (v29, 14 Oct 2026 copy) puts "Delete Part" at the footer's left (S13-R6) and sets the status with Part Status and Save (S13-R20 to S13-R22); that path is covered by Story 13's cases. Re-checked against v29 on 14 Oct 2026: still no basis.

notes: Story vs PRD (stories unchanged since 9 Oct; the PRD wins): SV-10814 has no S1-R9b (export follows search, filters and Supply filter; "Empty export"); SV-10824 still has the v27 S11-R3 ("where it can be edited and deleted"), the same acceptance criterion, and no S11-R3c; SV-10825 still has the v27 S12-R4 and no S12-R14a or S12-R14b. Cases follow PRD v29.

Design vs PRD (board 7.2 and canvas note library-note-2): board 7.2 matches v29 (no Delete on the detail page; the blue pencil-with-lines icon beside the name). The canvas note under 7.2 still says the entry "can be edited and deleted (S11-R3)" there, the v27 wording. No board shows the "Edit Library Part" window, its bottom-left Delete, the disabled state or its hover text (S11-R3, S11-R3c), "Empty export" (S1-R9b) or a "Part Library · {vendor}" result (S12-R14). Not conflicts; those results follow the PRD only.

Design vs PRD (boards 4.3, 4.6, 4.9): the line "N records selected." under the table in bulk mode is design-only; the tech plan (D24) adopts it, and C154757, C425594 and C425596 check it from that tech-plan quote, not from the PRD.

Design vs PRD (board 6.1): the design offers an active stocked part twice in the lookup (from inventory and from the Part Library). S12-R10 only names the shared-list result's source, so C425623 does not assume two results.

PRD wording vs screen (S12-R6): the PRD names "Administration → Roles & Permissions → Edit Role"; the app's menu reads Settings → Roles & Permissions (playbook). C154834, C425625 and C425626 use the screen's words.

Tech plan vs PRD (informs only): the tech plan (written against PRD v22) has no disabled Delete or hover text on a Part Library entry (S11-R3c) and still lists the Critical Reorder rules S5-R14 and S9-E12; cases follow PRD v29.

Story vs PRD (SV-11040, Verify Phase 3): the checklist line "Blocked parts show the disabled button with its tooltip (S2-E1…E4)" has no PRD basis (S2-E1: the change still goes through). No case follows it.
Tech plan only (C425602): "the confirmation stays open" after a bulk server error comes from the tech plan (Phase 3); the PRD is silent. It stays in the case as a tech-plan expectation.

Question for Product (S5-E3, C425603): v29 says a core's history shows on "the core's own Part History page", but the core has no row on the Inventory list, so a tester cannot open that page from the screens. How should a tester reach it? Until answered, C425603 marks the core's status "not checked by hand" and the Claude part reads the page by its address.

Open point (C425620): v29 disables Delete while a part uses the entry (S11-R3c), so the in-use refusal (S12-R11, §8 row) is produced with two tabs. The PRD does not say whether an open "Edit Library Part" window updates its Delete button without a reload; the case marks the refusal "not checked by hand" if it does.

Coverage note (S12-R14a): "in the last 12 months" and "not a core" cannot be produced by hand on fresh data (a delivery older than 12 months, a core received on a special-order line). They are quoted in C425624, A-N5, A-N6 and A-N7 but have no case of their own.

Coverage note (S11-R6): new Part Library entries are shown for creating an inventory part (C154830), the parts CSV import (C154830), a part request when received (C425616) and a delivery receipt (C540877). "A core charge", "returning a special-order part to inventory" and "returning a core to inventory" are quoted but have no case of their own: the PRD does not say how a tester sees those entries.

Coverage note (S12-R11): "Part Library entry not found" (no period), "... for ID: {id}." and "... for part number: {part number}." cannot be produced from the screens; they are quoted in C425620 and C425621, and C425622's setup doc lets a Claude session send the refused requests.

Fact for build verification (A-N3): on earlier builds the report exports show "Empty export" with a second line "Export didn't yield any results" (playbook). The PRD names only "Empty export" for the Inventory export; A-N3 requires those words and no file, and records any second line.
Pre-deployment data: C154753, C154831, C154835, C425625 and C425626 need records made before the Part Lifecycle build is deployed to the environment they run on.

Retire OR retest section (54275): C154761 stays proposed for retirement (re-checked against v29). C425629 is rewritten to the v29 import rule (S7-N10) and can leave the section if the QA lead agrees; C425602, C425622, C425701, C425723, C425755 and C425776 are re-stamped to v29 with no other change and stay in the section.
